page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-lssd-metal is a bare-metal server configuration engineered for resource-intensive enterprise computing. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors running at 4.2 GHz across 144 physical cores and 288 vCPUs. The hardware features a massive 504 MB L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AMX, AVX-512, and AVX-VNNI. The system is equipped with 2232 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per physical core. Storage is handled locally via six integrated NVMe SSDs totaling 19326 GB of capacity. The configuration does not include discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data demonstrates top-tier multi-threaded and memory performance. The instance achieved top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU testing (313,266.86) and PassMark CPU evaluations (178,741.62), reinforced by strong scores in cryptographic and extended instruction workloads. Memory throughput is a key differentiator, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching 1,090.21 GB/sec and write bandwidth reaching 412.25 GB/sec. Data processing capability is reflected in Redis SET throughput exceeding 422 million operations per second and high-throughput static web serving at 167.86 GB/sec. Conversely, Geekbench multi-core scores and small-model LLM text generation latency place in average to lower percentiles, highlighting that performance is optimized for highly parallelized multi-threaded architectures rather than consumer-style synthetic loads.

From an efficiency standpoint, the c4-highmem-288-lssd-metal delivers substantial density by combining 288 dedicated execution threads, over two terabytes of DDR5 RAM, and nearly 20 TB of local NVMe storage within a single bare-metal deployment. This eliminates virtualization overhead and reduces operational sprawl for workloads that require heavy internal communication. The server is well suited for large in-memory databases, high-capacity Redis deployments, large-scale Clang compilation jobs, data warehousing, and intensive multi-threaded ETL pipelines.
